requirements.name: 5.1.6 Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary
requirements.description: Mounting service account tokens inside pods can provide an avenue for privilege escalation attacks where an attacker is able to compromise a single pod in the cluster. Avoiding mounting these tokens removes this attack avenue.

requirements.name: 5.2.1 Minimize the admission of privileged containers
requirements.description: Privileged containers have access to all Linux Kernel capabilities and devices. A container running with full privileges can do almost everything that the host can do. This flag exists to allow special use-cases, like manipulating the network stack and accessing devices. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit privileged containers.

requirements.name: 5.2.2 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host process ID namespace
requirements.description: A container running in the host's PID namespace can inspect processes running outside the container. If the container also has access to ptrace capabilities this can be used to escalate privileges outside of the container. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit containers to share the host PID namespace.

requirements.name: 5.2.3 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host IPC namespace
requirements.description: A container running in the host's IPC namespace can use IPC to interact with processes outside the container. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit containers to share the host IPC namespace.

requirements.name: 5.2.4 Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host network namespace
requirements.description: A container running in the host's network namespace could access the local loopback device, and could access network traffic to and from other pods. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit containers to share the host network namespace.

requirements.name: 5.2.5 Minimize the admission of containers with allowPrivilegeEscalation
requirements.description: A container running with the `allowPrivilegeEscalation` flag set to true may have processes that can gain more privileges than their parent. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit containers to allow privilege escalation. The option exists (and is defaulted to true) to permit setuid binaries to run.

requirements.name: 5.2.6 Minimize the admission of root containers
requirements.description: Containers may run as any Linux user. Containers which run as the root user, whilst constrained by Container Runtime security features still have a escalated likelihood of container breakout. There should be at least one PodSecurityPolicy (PSP) defined which does not permit root users in a container.

requirements.name: Namespaces should have a default network policy to deny all egress traffic
requirements.description: Administrators should use a default policy selecting all Pods to deny all egress traffic and ensure any unselected Pods are isolated. Additional policies could then relax these restrictions for permissible connections.

requirements.name: Namespaces should have a default network policy to deny all ingress traffic
requirements.description: Administrators should use a default policy selecting all Pods to deny all ingress traffic and ensure any unselected Pods are isolated. Additional policies could then relax these restrictions for permissible connections.

requirements.name: Network policies should not have a default policy to allow all egress traffic
requirements.description: Administrators should use a default policy selecting all Pods to deny all ingress and egress traffic and ensure any unselected Pods are isolated. An 'allow all' policy would override this default and should not be used.  Instead, use specific  policies to relax these restrictions only for permissible connections.

requirements.name: Network policies should not have a default policy to allow all ingress traffic

requirements.name: Seccomp profile is set to docker/default in CronJob definition
requirements.description: In CronJob definition seccomp profile should be set to docker/default. Seccomp (secure computing mode) is used to restrict the set of system calls applications can make, allowing cluster administrators greater control over the security of workloads running in the cluster. Kubernetes disables seccomp profiles by default for historical reasons. It should be enabled to ensure that the workloads have restricted actions available within the container.
